title: Aug 19, 2026 | AI USER SKILLS | Practical AI Tips With Roger for Grant Beginners Our Team Experts
body:
Roger conducted a training session on using AI tools for grant prospecting, focusing on a specialized template he developed for finding government offices and nonprofit organizations that provide free assistance rather than traditional grants. He demonstrated how to use the template by copying it from the Lesko platform, filling in required information like applicant type, location, and specific help needed, and then using it as a prompt in AI assistants like ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Gemini. Roger explained the differences between seeking "assistance" (which includes free funding with no strings attached) versus "grants" (which require specific project proposals and reporting), noting that most participants are looking for assistance rather than traditional grants. He also covered best practices for using AI tools effectively, including managing token limits in free versions, avoiding fabrications, and proper prompt construction to get accurate results. The session included a live demonstration of using ChatGPT's voice feature and practical tips for following up with the organizations identified through AI searches.

Open the replay in Zoom

What's covered

  • Grant Prospecting with AI Tools — Roger led a meeting about grant prospecting with AI, demonstrating the Lesko platform's grant researcher tool and explaining its limitations compared to a custom template he would present later. He showed how the current tool provides broad categories like health, business, and cars, which may not specifically address individual needs, whereas his upcoming template would allow users to input specific problems and narrow down to relevant government offices and nonprofit organizations. The meeting included a brief interruption from Charity who joined virtually but had to leave early for medical appointments.
  • Grant Prospecting Prompt Demonstration — Roger demonstrated how to use the grant prospecting prompt in call sheet classes, explaining that participants need to copy the template onto their own documents and modify sections A through F with specific details about their location and applicant type. He showed how to properly copy and paste the content using keyboard shortcuts, and explained that the prompt includes provisions for creating a calling script and a Spanish version if needed. Roger also provided background information about AI language models, explaining the distinction between LLMs and MLMs, and mentioned that some tools like Perplexity serve as aggregators that connect to other LLMs.
  • AI Assistants and Tool Overview — Roger explained the differences between LLMs and aggregators, highlighting the top four AI assistants: ChatGPT, Claude, Google Gemini, and Perplexity. He demonstrated a comprehensive list of 250 AI tools and recommended subscribing to at least one of the top four platforms, with Roger personally subscribing to three for $60 monthly. The conversation ended with Roger introducing a template for searching government offices and nonprofits, explaining how to customize the search parameters based on individual or business needs.
  • AI Prompt Template for Organizations — Roger explained how to use a detailed AI prompt template to search for government offices and nonprofit organizations that provide assistance. He demonstrated the key sections of the template including applicant information, location details, help description, and specific instructions for resource types and search parameters. Roger emphasized the importance of being specific about what types of organizations to include or exclude, setting proper priority levels, and using anti-repeat rules to ensure unique results. He also discussed how to handle potential AI fabrication issues by including specific policies in the prompt to prevent made-up information.
  • AI Grant Prospecting Implementation — Roger and Pitts discussed implementing an AI grant prospecting prompt, clarifying that the entire prompt should be copied into the designated section without filling out the A, B, C, D, E, F fields separately. Roger explained that the professional designation should be used to ensure the AI treats the request seriously and provides expert-level assistance. They also discussed creating additional files like voice files and belief files to help the AI better understand personal preferences and positions, though these are optional and can be modified as needed.
  • Grants vs Assistance Programs — Roger discussed the distinction between grants and assistance programs, explaining that assistance programs typically involve direct payments or forgiveness loans with no requirement to report back, while grants require specific purposes and reporting obligations. He emphasized the importance of asking for "help" rather than "grants" when seeking funding, and advised that eligibility requirements and available resources should be clearly understood before applying. Roger also shared his involvement in a group called CE5 that practices consciousness exercises for communicating with extraterrestrials, though this was not directly related to the main discussion about funding resources.
  • AI Impact on Jobs Discussion — Roger discussed the impact of AI on jobs, explaining how AI is replacing both white-collar and blue-collar positions and emphasizing the need for humans to focus on tasks that machines cannot perform. He demonstrated various AI tools like ChatGPT and discussed their features, including voice capabilities and subscription tiers. Roger also shared tips for effectively using AI tools and provided a historical perspective on how productivity and job roles have evolved over time.

title: Aug 19, 2026 | PAY MY DEBT & BILLS | Learn How to Find Grants to Pay Your Debt and Bills
body:
The meeting, led by Tony from Let's Go Help, focused on helping members navigate resources for paying debts and bills. Tony walked through the "Pay My Debt and Bills" space, demonstrating how to use HUD.gov to find free, vetted financial counselors and emphasizing the importance of gathering necessary documents before reaching out for help. He discussed strategies for negotiating with creditors and understanding rights under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act. Members Martin and Laura received live demonstrations of the HUD counselor search tool using their zip codes. Tony also showed how to use the site's grant researcher tool to find organizations that could assist with specific needs, such as paying a water bill or legal help for a timeshare. The conversation also touched on student loan forgiveness myths and the challenges facing educators.

Open the replay in Zoom

What's covered

  • New Member Onboarding Session — Tony led a session on "Pay My Debt and Bills Live" for new members, welcoming Billy and Martin as new participants. He guided attendees through the roadmap feature and emphasized completing their profiles, including location and time zone information. Tony explained the structure of the Quick Guide Library, distinguishing between courses and quick guides, and provided an overview of HUD's free financial counseling services available across the United States.
  • Financial Assistance Resource Consultation — Tony conducted a consultation with Martin to help her find financial assistance resources in North Carolina. Martin indicated she was interested in home buying, home improvements, and rental housing services, and expressed concerns about potential fair housing rights violations. Tony provided guidance on using a HUD-approved resource list containing 31 organizations, recommending that Martin focus on non-profit organizations (.org domains) that offer credit workshops for the best results. The consultation concluded with Tony confirming Martin's contact information and expressing appreciation for her military service.
  • Veterans Assistance Resources Discussion — Tony discussed resources available for veterans and emphasized the importance of being prepared with necessary documentation before contacting assistance programs. He advised attendees to gather copies of identification, bank statements, and bills, and to consult multiple experts rather than relying on a single source. Tony also warned against debt scams and encouraged participants to use government-approved resources for assistance.
  • Debt Management Strategies Discussion — Tony led a discussion on debt management strategies, covering how to negotiate with creditors, understand consumer rights, and handle debt collection practices. He emphasized contacting creditors directly before seeking external help and warned against debt settlement scams. Tony also explained the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, highlighting protections against harassment and legal timeframes for debt collection. He encouraged participants to reach out for additional resources if needed and offered to share more detailed strategies with those in specific situations.
  • Counseling Session Resource Matching — Tony conducted a counseling session with Laura to assess her needs and match her with appropriate resources. Laura indicated she was interested in buying a home, home improvements, and financial management services, and preferred video counseling sessions. Tony provided recommendations including Operation Hope and other local organizations based on Laura's location in Baltimore, Maryland, and explained the platform's features including the welcome tour and call sheet classes.
  • AI Grant Researcher Tool Training — Tony explained how to use the AI Grant Researcher tool to find organizations that can help with specific needs, demonstrating the process with Laura's example of needing help paying water bills in Baltimore, Maryland. He noted that while the tool works well for single needs, staff assistance is recommended for complex cases involving multiple criteria. Tony mentioned upcoming classes including an AI Workshop on Fridays and an AI User Skills class hosted by Roger, where participants can learn to incorporate AI into their daily lives and business searches.
  • New Action Plan Tool Demonstration — Tony demonstrated how to use a new tool for Laura that creates action plans and call sheets with hyperlinks to organizations for assistance with water bills. He showed Laura how to access and use the tool, including switching between action plans and call sheets using tabs. When Linda asked about getting help with timeshare issues, Tony suggested using the grant researcher tool to find free legal assistance and offered to run a search for her specific location.
  • Federal Student Loan Updates — Tony led a discussion on federal student loans, addressing questions from Sunny about recent changes and requirements. He explained that borrowers have a 90-day window to switch to a new repayment plan, and emphasized that studentaid.gov is the only official source for federal loan relief. Tony advised Sunny to create or log into her account to review her current status and apply for any necessary changes.
  • Federal Student Loan Relief Options — Tony advised Sunny that the only official way to get relief on federal student loans is through studentaid.gov, and recommended two non-profit organizations for additional help: the Institute of Student Loan Advisors and StudentLoanBorrowingAssistance.org. The discussion explored whether a data breach involving Department of Education information could provide a legal basis for loan forgiveness, with Tony clarifying that while complaints can be filed, no statutory mechanism exists to discharge debt based on privacy violations alone. Tony emphasized that any third-party services charging fees for this type of assistance are likely scams, and warned that student loan debt cannot be written off through bankruptcy.
  • Education Security and Challenges Discussion — The group discussed concerns about Elon Musk's access to education department data and the potential security implications of this arrangement. The conversation then shifted to broader challenges in education, including teacher shortages, poor working conditions, and the impact of technology on students. Participants agreed that addressing teacher pay and improving school leadership were key issues that needed attention, with some emphasizing the role of parents in supporting educational improvements.
  • Arizona Education and Legal Updates — Sharron and Tony discussed the closure of public schools in Arizona and the resulting increase in alternative education options, including charter schools, private schools, micro schools, and homeschooling. They also talked about the challenges teachers face with disruptive behavior from students and the current teacher shortage. Tony provided information about debt collection laws, specifically the requirement for debt validation within the first 30 days of a debt being sold to a third-party collector. The conversation ended with Tony announcing upcoming live events, including a clinic and welcome tour scheduled for the following day.

title: Find Free and Low-Cost Health Services
body:
Getting the healthcare you need shouldn’t be overwhelming or expensive. The good news? There are thousands of free and low-cost clinics that provide medical, dental, mental health, and substance use care—you just need to know where to look.

This lesson will guide you to the best resources for accessing affordable health care options near you.

 1. Watch Matthew's Video First 

 2. Find Free and Low-Cost Clinics Near You 

Many nonprofit organizations and government programs offer free or low-cost healthcare services. Here’s how to get started:

  • 🔎 SEARCH | Visit NeedyMeds.org and explore their Healthcare Savings section to find:

  • Medical clinics

  • Dental clinics

  • Mental health clinics

  • Substance use disorder clinics

  • 📝 LOCATE | Use the clinic directory to find options near you and check their website for eligibility, services, and appointment availability.

  • 📧 CHECK EMAIL | After reaching out, you’ll receive an email with appointment details for in-person, phone, or online consultations.

  • 📁 GATHER INFORMATION | organize your medical history, medications, and any questions about your health concerns before your appointment.

💡 TIP: Keep all medical records and documents in one folder for easy access.

 3. Apply for Low-Cost or Free Health Insurance 

Even if you don’t think you qualify, 4 out of 5 applicants find coverage for less than $10 per month.

  • ✅ Visit HealthCare.gov to explore affordable insurance plans.

  • ✅ Get Free Help | Find Navigators or Certified Application Counselors who assist with applications at no cost:

    • 🔗 Find Free Application Help

    • 🚫 Avoid Agents & Brokers | These professionals work for insurance companies and may only offer plans that benefit them.

 4. Find Free Mental Health Support 

Mental health care is just as important as physical health. The government offers a judgment-free hotline to connect you with free or low-cost counselors:

  • 📞 Call 988 | Speak with a counselor online or schedule an in-person appointment near you.

  • 🔗 Visit 988Lifeline.org for more information.

 5. Learn About Clinical Trials for Free Care 

If traditional healthcare isn't working for you, clinical trials provide free access to cutting-edge treatments.

  • 🔬 Explore ClinicalTrials.gov to find government-funded studies on new treatments and procedures.

    • ✔ Free treatment & care

    • ✔ Access to top specialists

    • ✔ Compensation for travel & participation

  • 💰 $50 billion is spent annually on clinical trials, providing free treatment by top doctors and researchers.

 6. Understand Your Medicare Benefits 

If you’re on Medicare, new benefits and changes happen frequently. Free experts are available to help explain what you’re entitled to.

  • 📞 Call 877-839-2675 to speak with a Medicare expert.

  • 🔗 Visit SHIPHelp.org and find local Medicare advisors in your state.

 7. Find Local Health Services in Your Area 

For more free healthcare services in your area:

  • 🌎 Go to FindHelp.org: Enter your ZIP code and click the Health tab to see available options.

👉 There are over 215 sources of free healthcare in some areas—find out what’s available near you!

GET STARTED NOW ☟

Key Resources for Finding Low-Cost Health Care

  • 🔗 Find Free Clinics & Prescriptions – NeedyMeds

  • 🔗 Apply for Affordable Health Insurance – HealthCare.gov

  • 🔗 Find Free Application Help – Certified Navigators

  • 🔗 Mental Health Support – 988 Lifeline 📞 Call: 988

  • 🔗 Find a Clinical Trial for Free Treatment – ClinicalTrials.gov

  • 🔗 Medicare Help & Benefits – SHIP Help 📞 Call: 877-839-2675

  • 🔗 Find More Local Health Services – FindHelp.org

These free and low-cost resources can help you stay healthy without breaking the bank. Start searching today! 🚀

title: Get Help With Paying Your Medical Bills
body:
Even if you have insurance, medical expenses can pile up fast. But there are grants and assistance programs that can help cover out-of-pocket costs, prescription drugs, co-pays, and even living expenses while you're sick.

This lesson will guide you to nonprofit and government programs that provide free financial assistance for medical costs.

 1. Watch Matthew's Video First 

These programs are part of the "giving economy"—a network of government offices and nonprofit organizations that distribute funds for free. Unlike companies you might find through Google, these organizations exist to help you, not to charge you.

 2. Contact These Key Organizations for Health Care Financial Assistance 

 ➽ Apply for Grants to Cover Medical Expenses 

Many programs offer grants to help pay for treatments, prescriptions, and other health-related expenses.

  1.  GOOD DAYS   🔗 Website | Covers medical expenses not paid by insurance (Income eligibility up to $160,000).

  2.  PAN FOUNDATION   🔗 Website | It covers out-of-pocket prescription drug costs.

  3.  PATIENT ADVOCATE CO-PAY RELIEF   🔗 Website | Offers grants for insurance co-pays when visiting doctors or hospitals.

 ➽ Get One-on-One Help Managing Your Medical Bills 

If you're struggling with medical bills, these services offer free case management to help reduce costs and navigate insurance issues.

  •  PATIENT ADVOCATE CASE MANAGEMENT   🔗 Website | One-on-one case management to fight high medical bills.

  •  INSURANCE DENIALS & APPEALS   🔗 Website | Free assistance to appeal an insurance denial or unfair medical billing.

 ➽ Get Financial Assistance for Living Expenses While Sick 

If you're too sick to work, you may qualify for help covering rent, utilities, and other essentials.

  •  FINANCIAL RESOURCE DIRECTORY   🔗 Website | Find 50-100 local sources of financial support while ill.

  •  HELP FOR CAREGIVERS  🔗 Website | Provides financial support for family caregivers who must take time off work.

 ➽ Disease-Specific Grants & Financial Assistance 

Some organizations provide funding specifically for people with chronic or serious conditions like cancer, diabetes, asthma, and rare diseases.

  •  PAN FOUNDATION    🔗 Website | Search for disease-specific financial aid programs.

 ➽ Find a Support Group for Your Condition 

Support groups can connect you with others facing similar challenges, as well as additional financial resources.

  •  FIND A HEALTH SUPPORT GROUP  🔗 Website | Search for thousands of health-related support groups.

 ➽ Additional Organizations Offering Free Money & Help 

If the above organizations don’t have funds, try these additional nonprofits:

  • 🔗 Accessia Health

  • 🔗 TAF Cares

  • 🔗 CancerCare

  • 🔗 HealthWell Foundation

  • 🔗 Leukemia & Lymphoma Society (LLS)

  • 🔗 National Organization for Rare Disorders

 TIP: How to Approach These Organizations 

  • 📞 CALL FIRST: Most grants require direct contact before applying. Call and explain your medical expenses.

  • 💪 BE PERSISTENT: If one program is out of funds, keep asking—there are many organizations to help.

  • 🚫 AVOID GOOGLE SCAMS: For-profit companies may charge fees for grant applications—stick to nonprofit and government-backed resources.

START CALLING & APPLYING NOW! ☟

Key Resources for Getting Financial Help for Medical Costs

  • 🔗 Grants for Medical Bills – Good Days

  • 🔗 Prescription Drug Grants – PAN Foundation

  • 🔗 Co-Pay Assistance – Patient Advocate Co-Pay Relief

  • 🔗 One-on-One Medical Bill Help – Patient Advocate Case Management

  • 🔗 Financial Aid While Sick – Financial Resource Directory

  • 🔗 Help for Caregivers – Caregiver Assistance

  • 🔗 Disease-Specific Grants – PAN Fund Finder

  • 🔗 Find a Support Group – Mayo Clinic Groups

If you’re struggling with medical costs, these financial aid programs can provide relief. Start applying today! 🚀

title: LESSON 2 | 18 THINGS EVERY SENIOR SHOULD KNOW (STARTING AT 40!)
body:
The programs listed below are restricted to seniors.
BUT — as a senior, you are ALSO eligible for programs that have NO age restrictions!

That means you can also apply for programs that help you:

✔ Pay Your Bills
✔ Get Out of Debt
✔ Start a Business
✔ Buy a Home
✔ Get Legal Help
✔ Get Health Care

Being a senior doesn’t limit you — it EXPANDS your options!

➽ 1 | Over 40? YOU’RE PROTECTED!

If you’re 40 or older, it’s ILLEGAL to discriminate against you because of age.

Think you were treated unfairly at work? FILE A COMPLAINT FOR FREE!

👉 https://www.eeoc.gov/filing-charge-discrimination
📞 1-800-669-4000

Don’t guess. ASK!

➽ 2 | Free Legal Help for ANY Problem

You don’t need money to get legal help.

Call the Eldercare Locator — they connect you to FREE local help.

👉 https://eldercare.acl.gov/home
📞 800-677-1110

One phone call could change everything.

➽ 3 | Property Tax Too High?

Many states LOWER or FREEZE property taxes for seniors!

Call your local property tax office.
Or check:
👉 https://ptaconsumers.aarpfoundation.org/

Why pay more than you have to?

➽ 4 | Confused About Medicare?

STOP guessing!

There are FREE experts who will compare plans for you — at no cost.

👉 https://www.shiphelp.org/

Unbiased. Free. Smart.

➽ 5 | Need Home Repairs?

Grants and free repair programs are everywhere — but you have to ASK!

Go to 👉 FindHelp.org
Type your ZIP code
Search “Seniors”

You may be shocked how much help is there!

➽ 6 | Caregiver Money Is Available

Taking care of someone?
There may be FUNDING and SUPPORT programs for you.

👉 https://eldercare.acl.gov/home
📞 800-677-1110

Or search FindHelp.org
Put in your ZIP code
Use the keyword: “Caregiver”

Sample for Kensington, MD 20895
454 Programs Provide Free Funding and Services In this area
https://findhelp.org/search/text?term=senior&postal=20895

Free money is real — but only if you look!

➽ 7 | Want Someone to Walk You Through Everything?

Call Eldercare Locator.
They literally get paid to help you find help.

📞 800-677-1110

Use them!

➽ 8 | Free Tax Preparation

Why pay to file taxes?

The IRS sponsors FREE tax help for seniors.

👉 https://freetaxassistance.for.irs.gov/s/sitelocator

Keep your money!

➽ 9 | Government Pays to Hire Seniors

YES — there’s a federal program that pays organizations to train and hire older workers!

👉 https://www.careeronestop.org/LocalHelp/EmploymentAndTraining/find-older-worker-programs.aspx
📞 1-877-872-5627

Experience is POWER!

➽ 10 | Free College at 60?

Many states offer FREE or cheap college starting around age 60.

You could live another 20–30 years.
Why not do something FUN this time?

👉 https://www.aarp.org/work/careers/free-college-classes/

➽ 11 | College With No Age Limit? Even Better!

Many community colleges offer FREE training programs — NO AGE REQUIREMENT.

👉 https://www.careeronestop.org/LocalHelp/CommunityServices/find-community-colleges.aspx

New career? Higher pay? Why not?

➽ 12 | 55–80+? Get Paid to Volunteer Abroad

The Peace Corps LOVES older applicants!

Short-term. Long-term.
Living expenses and healthcare included.

👉 https://www.peacecorps.gov/faqs/older-applicants/

Adventure doesn’t expire!

➽ 13 | Find EVERYTHING in Your ZIP Code

Go to 👉 FindHelp.org
Type your ZIP
Search “Seniors”

Hundreds of programs may pop up.

If you don’t look, you don’t get.

Sample for Kensington, MD 20895
974 Programs Provide Free Funding and Services In this area
https://findhelp.org/search/text?term=senior&postal=20895

➽ 14 | Call Your Elected Officials

Having trouble with a government office?

Call your elected representative.
They have staff whose JOB is to fix problems for voters.

👉 https://www.commoncause.org/find-your-representative/

They work for YOU.

➽ 15 | Stick with .GOV and .ORG

.GOV and .ORG = help
.COM = usually selling something

Not always bad — just be smart.

Free help lives in government and nonprofit offices.

➽ 16 | Your Phone Is Your SUPERPOWER 📞

The real secret?

CALL.

Call the nonprofits.
Call the government offices.
Ask questions.

They get paid to help you.

Yes, you may wait on hold.
Yes, you may need patience.

But FREE MONEY and FREE HELP are worth it.

🚀 THE BIG SECRET

The help is out there.

title: Welcome to the Ask a Question Feed!
body:
This is your space for personalized support on navigating medical bills, financial assistance, and healthcare costs. Whether you need help finding grants, disputing medical charges, negotiating bills, or accessing insurance benefits, you'll find expert guidance here.

How to Ask a Question?

  • Post Your Question – Be as specific as possible. Instead of asking, “How do I get help with medical bills?” try, “Are there grants available for [my condition] in [my state]?”
  • Team Support – Our team specializes in medical debt relief, healthcare grants, and insurance advocacy. Look for their responses, which are easily identifiable by the colored background behind their names in the feed.
  • Timely Responses – We aim to reply quickly, but response times may vary due to time zones and question volume. Thank you for your patience—we’ll get back to you soon!
  • Follow-Up Questions – Need more details? Feel free to ask follow-up questions to ensure you have all the necessary information.

Tips for Getting the Best Support

  • Complete the Step-by-Step Guide First – Go through the full course to build a strong foundation before asking questions.
  • Do Your Research First – Check out the community’s reports and guides for key insights before posting.
  • Be Specific – The clearer your question, the more detailed and helpful our response can be.
  • Stay Engaged – Follow up on advice, share progress, and keep the conversation going to get the most out of this space.

We’re Here to Help

This feed is designed to make your medical bill relief journey smoother, so don’t hesitate to ask for guidance. No question is too small or too big—your financial well-being is our priority.

Start by posting your question today, and let us help you take the next step toward reducing your medical expenses!

title: Learn How to Get a Free Financial Counselor Appointment
body:
If you're struggling with debt or keeping up with bills, you're not alone. The stress of financial problems can affect your health, peace of mind, and overall well-being. The good news? There’s free expert help available to guide you through the process. This lesson will show you where to start and how to avoid common pitfalls.

 1. Watch Matthews's video 


 2. Make an Appointment With Free Financial Counselor 

Many people turn to Google for debt relief, but this can lead to scams or costly services. Instead, start by connecting with a certified financial counselor—many of them offer free, government-funded support. These experts can help you assess your financial situation, prioritize your debts, and create a realistic plan to regain control.

Here’s how to find a trusted financial counselor:

  • 🔎 SEARCH | Visit HUD.gov/counseling and enter your zip code to find a HUD-approved financial counselor who specializes in debt management and credit counseling.

  • 📝LOCATE | Pinpoint the application or contact information on the website of the HUD-approved financial counselor you have chosen, and follow the steps indicated to start the process of acquiring a counselor.

  • 📧 CHECK EMAIL | A certified counseling agency will contact you to schedule an appointment—either in person, over the phone, or via Zoom Meeting.

  • 📁 GATHER INFORMATION | Prepare your financial documents, including bills, credit reports, and any notices from creditors.

💡 TIP: Create folders (digital or physical) to keep all your financial information organized and easily accessible.

 3. Seek Advice from More than One Expert 

Not all counselors have the same knowledge or access to resources. If one doesn’t provide the answers you need, don’t hesitate to contact another. There are multiple government-backed programs and nonprofit organizations available to help.

🚨 Stay Away from Debt Scams

Many online services charge fees for "debt relief" but fail to deliver. Some even engage in fraudulent practices. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) has banned over 450 debt relief companies from operating due to scams. Protect yourself by avoiding high-cost services and sticking to government-approved resources.

🔎 Use Trusted Websites for Financial Help

  • HUD Financial Counselors: HUD.gov/counseling

  • Consumer Financial Protection Bureau: consumerfinance.gov

  • Find Local Nonprofit Help: findhelp.org

Taking this first step—getting expert, free guidance—will set you on the right path to reducing your debt and managing your bills effectively.

💰 START SEARCHING NOW

title: Quick Tour of the Changes So Far
Welcome to the Lesko Help 2 Community!
body:
We are thrilled to welcome you to the Lesko Help 2 Community, where we work together to help individuals access government grants and free services available to the average person living in America. Our community is dedicated to empowering people by providing them with the knowledge and resources to access government programs that can change their lives.

What You’ll Get in the Lesko Help 2 Community

We’re here to:

  • Connect with each other through questions, prompts, live streams, and a weekly calendar.
  • Share our stories, experiences, and ideas.
  • Discover opportunities for grants and free services through our workshops, courses, events, and more.
  • Ultimately, achieve the results we want but are nearly impossible to get on our own without the support of a community.

We’re confident that this community will be an incredible resource for you.

Our Community Culture

Our community culture is based on a few key values:

  • Say hello and introduce yourself. We encourage all members to introduce themselves to the community. Use the introduction prompt in your profile to say hello and share a little about yourself.
  • Join in. Add your stories, experiences, and ideas to our prompts to make your time here as valuable as possible. We welcome questions and discussions related to government grants and free services.
  • Be supportive. We’re building something special here, and we need each other to be supportive and encouraging. Share your stories or experiences, but please refrain from giving advice or judgment. And obviously, don’t spam or promote.
  • Connect generously. A community only gets stronger and more valuable to each of us as we contribute and spark connections with other members. When people introduce themselves, say hello. Find people near you or with similar interests. Dash off a quick note or reaction that will make someone’s day—another great reason to download the mobile app!

Explore the Welcome Checklist.

We’ve added a Welcome Checklist to quickly give you the layout of the Lesko Help 2 Community—how to adjust your notifications, download the app, and more. You can find it in the main Activity Feed.

How to Ask Questions 💫

Step 1: 👉 Read How to Ask Questions

Step 2: 👉 Post Your Question in Ask You Questions Here

Step 3: 👉 Check the FAQ Page

💥 PS: Do not ask your questions in the comments below. 💥

We thank you. 🙏

title: 05-08-23 Staff Meeting
body:
Staff Meeting Notes

  1. Navigating scamming activity specifically-with the contests.

  2. Due to the removal of multiple items from the Welcome Checklist in LH2, the “Introduce Yourself” Feature is much more prominently displayed; because of this, we are seeing a Drastic Increase in Bios being created by the members. I had been starting to get us caught up in this area, back to October of ‘22, and now I can barely keep up with them.

  3. The items removed from the Welcome Checklist that need a New Home:

    1. All of our Applications (only the Giveaway was removed, but if we create a new space, having ALL applications in one space, maybe in the “Welcome!” Collection, would be useful).

    2. Payment Portal

    3. Our Hotline

    4. Emergency Resources List

    5. Emergency Mental Health Resources List

    6. Class Roster

  4. Things we still need in a Space somewhere:

    1. I would like to Add Matthew’s Meta Grants Report as more and more class members are requesting the information on how to locate the report.

    2. An About Us Section, Giulia began working on one, but it hasn’t been completed/released. In that I would like to include a list of the websites that Matthew has and the leskohelp@gmail.com email address.

    3. TroubleShooting Guide

  5. The New Areas that have been created have internal tabs labeled “Questions”, but no one in the staff is handling that area. I think rather than a “Chat” style internal tab, a Questions Feed where Members can Create Posts is Much More Manageable.

  6. Can we have a set of the “Welcome” Emails sent to everyone, so that I can show the class what to look for and so that everyone will be better prepared to direct members when there are questions?

  7. Members are telling me that they are not receiving confirmation emails when they are filling out their applications. This is a Feature that Google is supposed to provide if the form is set up that way, and I double checked all of the forms that I had access to, including one for a Giveaway, and the feature was properly set. We might warn members that there seems to be an issue in this regard.

  8. Are the Episodes in Lesko TV also hosted Live in LeskoHelp?

  9. There are a TON of other “Lesko” Networks on Mighty Networks. Matthew, have you created a bunch of additional Networks or are these Scam Artists?

Welcome to the Ask a Question Feed!
body:
This is your space for personalized support on finding a job, starting training, or building a new career path. Whether you need help locating free programs, applying for internships, accessing tech tools, or understanding how to get started, you’ll find real support here.

How to Ask a Question?

  • ✔ Post Your Question → Be as specific as you can. Instead of asking, “How do I find a job?” try, “Are there free training programs for [industry] in [my state]?”
  • ✔ Team Support → Our team specializes in job search strategies, career coaching, training programs, and funding. Look for answers from the team—easy to spot by the colored background behind their names.
  • ✔ Timely Responses → We aim to reply quickly, but response times can vary based on time zones and question volume. Thanks for your patience—we’ll get back to you as soon as we can.
  • ✔ Follow-Up Questions → Got more questions? Ask again—this space is here to help you move forward.

Tips for Getting the Best Support

  • ✔ Complete the Step-by-Step Guide First → Go through the action plan to build a strong foundation before posting.
  • ✔ Do Some Research First → Check the space’s free guides, programs, and reports before asking—your answer might already be there.
  • ✔ Be Clear and Specific → The more focused your question, the better and faster we can help.
  • ✔ Stay Engaged → Follow up, take action, and share updates to get the most from this space.

We’re Here to Help

This feed exists to make your job search easier, so don’t hesitate to ask. Whether you’re feeling stuck, overwhelmed, or just need clarity—we’ve got your back.

Post your first question now and take the next step toward a better job and a brighter future! 🚀

body:
Walk through the tools most members get stuck on — free legal help searches, the Member AI research tool, call sheets, and saving what you're given so you can find it again later. Helpful if you're new to the platform.

Open the replay in Zoom

What's covered

  • 1:12 — Finding free legal help — Where to look for local attorneys, legal aid and legal resource series when credit or business disputes have cost you money.
  • 11:08 — Running the AI research tool — How long a report takes, where saved results live, and how to pull up to 50 local offices for your topic.
  • 13:22 — LLC setup and bill help — What members report paying for state LLC filings, plus getting a call sheet for mortgage and bill assistance.
  • 23:00 — Finding posts sent to you — Search your own name to pull up every resource anyone has ever given you, then bookmark it for later.
  • 29:02 — Courses versus real contacts — Why lessons teach and call sheets deliver actual local phone numbers, plus the what-to-say scripts.

Jillmarie Stich

GOVERNMENT AND NONPROFIT ASSISTANCE LOCATOR — MASTER PROMPT =========================== SECTION: USER INPUT INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE USER Do not delete the bracketed letters. Type your information after the colon and one space. Complete all fields before submitting the prompt. Resource Type: [A]Government offices Recipient Category: [B]cancer patients County: [C]Scott State: [D]MN ZIP Code: [E]56011 Purpose of the Help You Need: [F]Help with credit card debt caused by paying for treatment. Do not edit anything below this line. =========================== SECTION: AI ROLE AND TASK You are an expert research consultant specializing in verified United States government offices and legitimate nonprofit organizations that provide public assistance. Your task is to identify and present exactly twenty-five real and verified organizations or offices that match the Resource Type identified as [A]. Your primary search arena will be the Web. In addition to the Web, appropriate entities you find in your existing database can be used. After the name of the organization/office, indicate "(Web)" or "(DB)" to show if you found the information on the Web or in your Database. If fewer than the requested twenty-five listings can be found, do not fabricate anything, but instead state that fact. This is an unlikely situation since you are to continually extend the search radius as needed. Each organization or office must provide assistance to the Recipient Category identified as [B]. Each organization or office must be located in, or explicitly serve, the County identified as [C], the State identified as [D], or the ZIP Code identified as [E]. If the County and/or State do not correspond to the ZIP Code or their is any doubt, only consider the ZIP Code. If the County is given without the State, use the ZIP Code to determine the State. If the State is given without the County or ZIP Code, give responses for the whole State. If no County or State are given, proceed based upon ZIP Code. If neither the County, nor State, nor ZIP Code is given, do not conduct the search and return the message, "Location information is missing." Each organization or office must be directly relevant to the Purpose of the Help Needed identified as [F]. If the items labeled [A], [B], or [F] are empty, do not conduct the search and return the message, "Please complete all required fields and resubmit." This output will be used by real people as a calling and contact worksheet. Accuracy, clarity, and reliability are mandatory. Number each search result. Write in clear, professional American English that can be understood by someone with an average high-school education. Avoid jargon, filler language, and promotional tone. =========================== SECTION: STRICT NO-FABRICATION POLICY These rules are mandatory and non-negotiable. SUBSECTION: ACCEPTABLE SOURCES Only the following sources may be used. Government offices using official federal, state, county, or city websites with .gov domains. Verified nonprofit organizations using .org domains that are IRS-recognized 501(c)(3) organizations and verifiable through Charity Navigator or Candid / GuideStar. Universities or hospitals using .edu domains only when they operate a real, publicly accessible assistance program. SUBSECTION: ABSOLUTE PROHIBITIONS You must not guess, infer, estimate, or fabricate any information. You must not invent organization names, program names, phone numbers, email addresses, websites, contact names, dollar amounts, eligibility rules, or service descriptions. You must not use placeholder data, sample data, 555 phone numbers, fake websites, patterned numbers, invented staff names, or invented program titles. SUBSECTION: WEBSITE VERIFICATION All websites must be real and functioning. If a website cannot be confirmed as real and functioning, write exactly the following text and nothing else. Website not verified SUBSECTION: MISSING INFORMATION HANDLING If a specific data field does not appear in a verified source, write exactly the single most appropriate phrase below, or leave the field blank. Not provided Unknown Unavailable No direct email listed Web form only Do not substitute wording. Do not explain. =========================== SECTION: SEARCH AREA RULES The primary search area is the ZIP Code identified as [E]. If twenty-five qualifying organizations cannot be found within that ZIP Code, expand the search outward in the following order only. First expand to the remainder of the County identified as [C]. Then expand to neighboring counties. Then expand to statewide programs within the State identified as [D]. All organizations must still be relevant to the stated purpose and must plausibly serve the intended recipient category. =========================== SECTION: REQUIRED OUTPUT STRUCTURE For each of the twenty-five organizations or offices, present the information using the following labeled fields, in this exact order. Organization or Office Name Website Email Address Phone Number Contact Name Direct Line or Extension Description of the Office or Organization Eligibility Requirements Description of Services Offered Typical Dollar Value of Available Services Maximum Amount of Grants or Loans Available Each field must appear on its own line with its label clearly written out. If multiple websites or phone numbers exist, list each on a separate line beneath the same label. =========================== SECTION: CALLING GUIDANCE FOR INEXPERIENCED USERS Include the following calling guidance with each organization or office. STANDARD OPENING SENTENCE Use this wording exactly. Hello, my name is ___. I’m calling to ask about assistance programs your office may offer and whether I might qualify. CALL GUIDANCE CONTENT Explain how the caller should describe the type of help they need based on the stated purpose. Explain how the caller should ask about eligibility requirements. Explain what documents or information the caller may need to prepare. Explain whether appointments, referrals, or walk-ins are required. Explain what the next step is, such as an application process or intake procedure. REQUIRED CLOSING QUESTION Use this wording exactly. Is there another office or organization you would recommend I contact as well? The tone must always be polite, respectful, and confident. Never frame the request as asking for “free help.” =========================== SECTION: COMPLETION REQUIREMENTS Do not stop early. Do not summarize. Do not provide fewer than twenty-five organizations or offices. Continue until all twenty-five entries are fully completed. If information cannot be verified for a particular field, apply the Missing Information Handling rules exactly.

body:
"Hello,
Good Morning to the New Member, that just joined Lesko Help 2, and Members!!! I hope everyone had a great weekend. This a reminder that we have class tonight The Lesko Weekly Live Basics, for those who are New to LeskoHelp & Lesko Help 2 and those who as struggling on WHO, WHERE, WHY, WHEN'S last but how I encourage all members to attend All the Lesko Training/Courses groups the here in Lesko Help 2 & utilize those chatrooms, it's a time/place to communicate with other members share resources with each other. I do attend all classes; I do share my experiences & share what I learned from my journey and hope to help other along the way.


-The Times/Event will locate on Report Tab on your Home landing Page, if you click the Event Tab, you will see the Upcoming Event, please select going so you can get a notification just before class starts. Same apples with LeskoHelp members. We ask that you Arrive on time at least 5-10mins early to set up, be patient sometimes it takes time getting, but not too long. If you havening issue getting in, I strongly encourage member start using their group chatroom, If have are you're coming in late we are asking that you try not disrupting class while in Instructor is in middle of lecture if all members can remember to put microphone on mute till towards the of class when the instructor always Q&A. *If you don't have a microphone capabilities you can type you're questions on live chat during the class but they will not be answered till Q&A is open.

*** LeskoHelp/Lesko Help 2 access for all both. Requirements:

  • *Facebook/Mighty Networks (Required)
  • *Install Zoom (Required)
  • *Install Mighty Networks (Required)
  • *Computer/Cell phone (Required)
  • *Internet (Required)

REMINDER: Members that are in the Partnership & Accountability Course

HOMEWORK ASSIGNMENT: Tonight's, assignment is if you are New to LeskoHelp & Lesko Help 2, if you haven't created a report, I want all students/members to make a list of what they want on their personal report, if you don't know what a personal report is or don't how where to start to create one. I really recommend you attending tonight's class, Students/ Member if you currently have a report and needs to be Updated, you will need to bring your report to class and you as well need to make a list of what you need to update on your report. If you already have your Personal Report Updated that's great, please bring to class as well. If you have questions locating your report, please tag Sabrina Giesler, I can assist finding your report not creating one.

I hope see all you member in class tonight, Have a great!!" Tammie Larson

title: 1-on-1 Help To Get Your Benefits (Recording)
Free Cars & Car Repairs
body:
1. Watch Matthew’s Video

2. Search for Free Car Programs in Your Area

Many local nonprofits and government programs offer:

  • Free vehicle giveaways

  • Free car repairs

  • Assistance with transportation needs

🔎 VISIT: findhelp.org

Steps:

🚗 Enter your zip code
🔎 Search “cars”

In one example shared:

  • One zip code showed 32 organizations offering car-related help.

  • Tampa, Florida showed 43 organizations.

Programs vary by:

  • Location

  • Available funding

  • Type of assistance

Your results will depend on where you live.

📞 The key step: Call the organizations directly.
Take the list and start contacting them to ask about eligibility and application steps.

3. Expand Your Search: Emergency Financial Assistance

If you do not immediately find a car-specific program, broaden your search.

A car repair is often considered an emergency expense — especially if you need transportation to work.

On findhelp.org:

📍 Enter your zip code
💵 Search “emergency financial assistance”

In the example shared, one area showed:

  • 40 programs under cars

  • 71 programs under emergency financial assistance

This widens your options significantly.

4. Important Strategy

  • Programs vary by city and funding levels.

  • Assistance is not guaranteed.

  • You must actively contact organizations.

  • Focus on nonprofit and government resources.

There are organizations designed to help people stay employed, care for their families, and overcome financial setbacks.

Start by searching locally, make the calls, and explore every available option.

title: LESSON 1
body:
1. Watch Matthew’s Video

2. Start With State Veteran Service Officers (Your First Stop)

Before applying anywhere else, connect with your State Veteran Service Officer (VSO).

🔎 VISIT: nacvso.org

Here’s what to do:

📍 Find your state
📞 Contact your local Veteran Service Officer
📄 Ask for help identifying and applying for all benefits you qualify for

Research has shown that Veteran Service Officers are often able to help veterans secure more benefits than anyone else. This makes them the strongest starting point.

3. Then Expand Beyond Veterans Benefits

Veterans benefits may only represent a small percentage of what is available overall. There are hundreds of thousands of additional programs that veterans and their families can qualify for.

🔎 VISIT: findhelp.org

Steps:

📍 Enter your zip code
🎖 Search “veterans”

In the example shared, one zip code produced 414 organizations offering free programs, including:

  • Veteran training programs

  • Aging and disability support for veterans

  • Iraq veteran services

  • Financial assistance

  • Support programs

Every organization listed provides free assistance — they do not charge fees.

4. Use All Available Benefit Categories

As a veteran, you may qualify for programs beyond traditional VA benefits, including:

  • Housing assistance

  • Rent support

  • Transportation help

  • Medical services outside the VA system

  • Training and education programs

If one office cannot help, move to another. There are many options.

5. Contact Your Elected Officials

Your elected officials have staff whose job is to help constituents access benefits. They track how many people they assist and often help resolve benefit issues.

Do not overlook this resource.

6. Avoid Paid Services

Be cautious of websites ending in .com that offer to help you get benefits — many charge fees or attempt to take a portion of your benefits.

Instead:

  • Use .org and .gov resources

  • Contact official Veteran Service Officers

  • Speak with organizations that are funded to help you — not businesses trying to sell services

Start with free, official resources. Veterans and their families should be first in line — but only if they know where to look.

title: LESSON 2 | 18 THINGS EVERY VETERAN SHOULD KNOW 🇺🇸
body:
(Most Veterans Forget to Apply for Billions in Benefits!)

The programs listed below are specifically for Veterans.

BUT — as a Veteran, you are ALSO eligible for programs that have NO military requirement!

That means you can also apply for programs that help you:
• Pay Your Bills
• Get Out of Debt
• Start a Business
• Buy a Home
• Get Legal Help
• Get Health Care

Being a Veteran doesn’t limit you — it EXPANDS your options!

➽ 1 | There’s $400+ Billion Just for Veterans

In 2026, Veterans Benefits total about $400 Billion.

The total benefits available to ALL Americans is over $5 Trillion.
Veterans receive only about 8% of that total.

If you don’t find what you need in VA programs, there are hundreds of billions more in non-veteran programs you can apply for.

Don’t stop at “No.”

➽ 2 | One Office Doesn’t Know Everything

No single person or office knows ALL the programs available.

If someone tells you “You don’t qualify,” that only means you don’t qualify for THAT program.

There are hundreds more. Keep asking.

➽ 3 | First Stop: County Veterans Service Office (FREE!)

Make an appointment.

📞 888-777-4443
https://nvf.org/veteran-service-officers/

They get paid to help YOU.

➽ 4 | Search 400+ Additional Programs in Seconds

Go to FindHelp.org
Type your ZIP code
Search “Veterans”

Sample: Kensington, MD 20895
https://findhelp.org/search/text?term=veterans&postal=20895

If you don’t search, you don’t see.

➽ 5 | Benefits Can Cover Your Family Too

Many programs help spouses, children, caregivers, and surviving family members.

Don’t assume it’s just for you. Ask.

➽ 6 | Help With Debt & Living Expenses

http://LeskoLovesAI.com/PayYourBills

➽ 7 | Starting or Expanding a Business?

http://LeskoLovesAI.com/Business

➽ 8 | Careers & Job Training

http://LeskoLovesAI.com/Career

➽ 9 | Housing & Real Estate Help

http://LeskoLovesAI.com/HomeBuyers

➽ 10 | Having Trouble With a Government Office?

Call your elected representative.

https://www.commoncause.org/find-your-representative/

They work for YOU.

➽ 11 | Stick with .GOV and .ORG

.GOV and .ORG usually mean real help.
.COM usually means someone is selling something.

Be smart.

➽ 12 | Your Phone Is Your SUPERPOWER 📞

CALL.
Call nonprofits.
Call government offices.
Ask questions.

They get paid to help you.

➽ 13 | Reapply If You Were Denied

Rules change. Income limits change. Your situation changes.

Try again.

➽ 14 | Use Multiple Sources

Layer your search:
County Office + FindHelp + Local nonprofits + State programs.

That’s how you uncover hidden help.

➽ 15 | There Are Local Programs No One Advertises

Small nonprofits. County emergency funds. City hardship programs.

Search your ZIP code and ASK.

➽ 16 | Don’t Assume You Make “Too Much”

Many programs have high income limits.

Apply anyway.

➽ 17 | You Served. You Earned This.

Benefits are not charity.
They are earned. They exist for you.

Use them.

➽ 18 | The Big Secret 🚀

The help is out there.
The money is out there.
The programs are out there.

Most people just don’t ask.

YOU are not most people.

title: Federal & Local Support for Small Business Owners
body:
Navigating business support programs can feel complicated—but you’re not alone. There are national offices and local agencies ready to help you get certified, find funding, and access free support.

This lesson will guide you through some of the most important federal and city-level resources you can use as a small business owner. Whether you’re looking for government contracts, certifications, or simply trying to locate your local support agency, this is a great place to start.

🧭 Federal Small Business Offices

These government-run offices are designed to support small business participation in federal programs, including funding, contracts, and training.

🔹 Federal Small Business Offices

Explore how to work with the U.S. Department of Defense and connect with federal small business representatives in various agencies.

📌 National Small Business Portals

These general portals can guide you to many different government services and small business tools:

🔹 USA.gov Small Business Portal

A great all-in-one resource for exploring small business programs, licenses, and government-run support.

🔹 MySBA Certifications

Looking to become a certified small business for federal contracts or programs? This is the official SBA platform to get started with certifications.

🗺 Local Government Tools: Find Help in Your Area

Local programs are often easier to access and more tailored to your needs. These tools will help you find your county, city, and regional offices, where additional grants, licenses, or support may be offered.

🔹 NACo County Explorer

Use this map-based tool to locate your county government, see what services they offer, and explore local small business programs.

🔹 National League of Cities

Find out what your city government is doing to support small business owners. Search for city-specific programs, grants, and initiatives that could apply to you.

📣 Your Next Move

Now that you have access to both federal-level and local-level tools, take a few minutes to:

  • Locate your city or county agency using the tools above.

  • Bookmark the SBA Certification Portal if you plan to work with government grants or contracts.

✔ In the next lesson, we’ll look at grant opportunities you can apply for now—from national programs to niche opportunities for underrepresented founders.

Let’s keep building!

title: 🤖 AI USER SKILLS | Practical AI Tips With Roger for Grant Beginners Our Team Experts
body:
Join Roger for an insightful weekly class where you’ll learn how to use AI tools for grant prospecting, set up your browser, build better prompts, and use AI in your daily searches.

Hello bright learner 💛

You’re invited to join Roger for a warm and practical training where you’ll learn how to use AI tools to make your grant searching easier, faster, and more effective.

In this program, you’ll learn how to set up your browser for AI tools, how to explore financial assistance opportunities (such as grants, direct payments, transfer payments, forgiveness, and loans you don’t pay back), and how to use simple prompt techniques to improve your AI results.
This session is beginner-friendly and gives you clear steps you can follow right away.

Why You’ll Love Joining

  • AI TOOL SETUP | Learn how to prepare your browser and install helpful AI tools

  • GRANT PROSPECTING | Use AI to search for grants and financial assistance options

  • PROMPT BASICS | Learn simple ways to write better prompts and get clearer answers

  • RESOURCES ON LH2 | See where to find your replays and training materials

  • EXTRA LEARNING | Get tips on how AI can help with writing, searching, and daily tasks

How to Get Ready

  • BE ON TIME | Join a few minutes early so setup instructions are easier to follow

  • CAMERA ON | Keep your camera on if you feel comfortable

  • COME PREPARED | Bring your browser (Chrome, Edge, or Firefox) and simple questions

  • STAY WITH US | Stay for the full hour — each part builds on the last

We’re here to help you feel confident using AI in your grant journey.
Looking forward to seeing you there 💛

To help you get oriented and moving confidently, we’ve organized your start into three simple stages:

🚀 1. Quick Start: Get Set Up in LH2

Set up your profile

Adjust your notification settings

Join and attend live events

Find key resources

Ask questions and engage with the community

This is your “how everything works” guide for LH2.

✅ 2. Welcome Checklist: Cover the Essentials

Next, move through the checklist to make sure you’ve completed all the important basics.

👉 Lesko Help 2 Welcome Checklist

title: AI GRANT PROSPECTING CALLING SCRIPT PROMPT ADDITION
body:
AI GRANT PROSPECTING CALLING SCRIPT PROMPT-2026-0624-001.txt

AI GRANT PROSPECTING CALLING SCRIPT PROMPT ADDITION

====================================

> > > BEGIN COPYING HERE >>>

CALLING SCRIPT GENERATOR - SYSTEM INSTRUCTIONS

Using the information already provided in this session - specifically the Applicant Type, Resource Type, and the issue described - generate a personal calling script as follows.

Do not search for anything. Do not produce any listings.

Generate the calling script only.

TONE AND STYLE:

Write in warm, natural, conversational language that sounds like a real person speaking - not a formal script. The caller may be nervous, inexperienced, or dealing with a difficult situation. The words should feel honest and human, easy to say out loud, and natural enough that the caller does not sound like they are reading from a page.

SCRIPT CONTENTS - PRODUCE IN THIS EXACT ORDER

YOUR CALLING SCRIPT

WHEN SOMEONE ANSWERS:

Write a natural opening of 3 to 5 sentences in which the caller greets the person, introduces themselves by first name placeholder [your name], briefly explains who they are based on the Applicant Type from this session, and describes what they are calling about based on the issue from this session. The opening should sound like something a real person would actually say - warm, a little humble, and to the point. End by asking if there is someone who can help or if they are speaking with the right person.

THINGS TO REMEMBER DURING THE CALL:

Speak slowly and clearly. It is fine to pause or ask them to repeat something if you did not understand.

Write down the name of the person you spoke with and the date and time of the call.

Ask: "What documents or information will I need in order to apply or get help?" Write down everything they say.

Ask: "Is there an application I can fill out online, or do I need to come in person?"

Ask: "Is there a waiting list? If so, how long is the wait right now?"

Whether they can help you or not, always ask: "Do you happen to know of any other offices or organizations that might be able to help me with this? I would really appreciate any suggestions."

Thank them sincerely before you hang up.

IF YOU GET VOICEMAIL:

Write a brief, natural voicemail message of 3 to 4 sentences. The caller states their name, their phone number placeholder [your number], and gives a plain one-sentence description of what they need help with based on the issue from this session. End warmly and ask for a callback.

SPANISH VERSION

Generate the complete Spanish version below the English version ONLY if the Spanish Script field from this session was set to Y.

Skip entirely if it was set to N or left blank.

SU GUION DE LLAMADAS (ESPAÑOL)

Translate the complete calling script above into natural, conversational Spanish. Do not translate word for word - write it the way a native Spanish speaker would naturally say it in a phone call. Maintain the same warm, humble, and human tone throughout.

<<< END COPYING HERE <<<
